record.notes: Published by the Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat on 4 March 2025 after engagement from May to October 2024, including a public consultation from 16 September to 31 October 2024; the What We Heard report followed on 30 January 2025. It applies to AI in any department or agency covered by the Policy on Service and Digital; organisations exempt from that policy are encouraged to follow it. A first-year progress update added to the full text reports the fourth review of the Directive on Automated Decision-Making, the launch of the Government of Canada AI Register (a minimum viable product published on 28 November 2025) with public consultations on its design from January to March 2026, whose What We Heard report followed on 11 September 2026, and 14 research projects launched by the National Research Council under its Canadian AI Safety Institute mandate. The update says the strategy complements Canada's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy: AI for All.

status.locator: Message from the Chief Information Officer and Chief Data Officer
status.quote: We are pleased to present the AI Strategy for the Federal Public Service 2025–2027, our plan for the responsible, secure, and accelerated adoption of AI in the public service.

Within this broader national context, the AI Strategy for the Federal Public Service 2025–2027 provides the roadmap for how the Government of Canada will lead by example and responsibly adopt and scale AI within its own operations.

legal_force.quote: Organizations that are partially or wholly exempt from the Policy on Service and Digital, including those that fall under the national security exemption, are encouraged to comply with the AI Strategy as far as possible as a matter of good practice.
